questions.q: Which Dockerfile instruction must always come first?
options: FROM
CMD
EXPOSE
WORKDIR
questions.explain: FROM sets the base image that every later instruction builds on top of, so it always comes first.

questions.q: What does the EXPOSE instruction actually do?
options: It opens the specified port so traffic can reach the container
It documents which port the app expects — it does not open the port itself
It installs a web server inside the image
It removes a port from the container's network interface
questions.explain: EXPOSE is documentation. Actually publishing a port to the host happens with the -p flag at `docker run`, covered in Lesson 4.

questions.q: Why does this lesson's Dockerfile copy requirements.txt and run pip install before copying the rest of the application code?
options: Python requires dependencies to be installed before any files exist
pip install only works in an empty directory
Docker's build cache reuses unchanged layers, so this keeps the dependency layer cached across code-only changes
It has no effect on build speed either way
questions.explain: Since the dependency layer sits above unchanged instructions, Docker reuses its cache on later builds unless requirements.txt itself changes — so an app code edit doesn't force a reinstall.

questions.q: What's the key difference between CMD and ENTRYPOINT?
options: They are functionally identical in every case
ENTRYPOINT only works with Python images
CMD can only be used once per Dockerfile, while ENTRYPOINT can be used multiple times
CMD is a default that arguments passed to `docker run` replace entirely; ENTRYPOINT is fixed, and those arguments get appended instead
questions.explain: Running `docker run my-app python debug.py` replaces a CMD entirely, but appends to a fixed ENTRYPOINT.

questions.q: In the complete example Dockerfile, how many total instructions does the final, real version use?
options: Three
Twelve
Seven
Twenty
questions.explain: FROM, WORKDIR, COPY, RUN, COPY, ENV, EXPOSE, and CMD — seven distinct instruction types across eight lines (COPY appears twice).
